research_question: Among children with conduct problems, what is the effect at the end of treatment of a personalised parenting or family intervention (tailored to the individual or adapted to a subgroup), compared with the standard non-personalised version of the same intervention, on mother-reported child conduct problems measured by the Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory (ECBI) Problem scale? Pool post-treatment arm-level means as a random-effects mean difference in ECBI Problem scale points, defined as personalised minus standard non-personalised intervention, so MD < 0 favours personalisation.
treatment_label: Personalised parenting or family intervention (individually tailored or adapted to a subgroup)
control_label: Standard non-personalised version of the same active parenting or family intervention
outcome_description: Child conduct problems measured specifically with the ECBI Problem scale at the first assessment after treatment ended. Extract the post-treatment mean, SD, and n for each randomised arm; use the mother's report when multiple reporters are available, and convert SE to SD where necessary. Do not include ECBI Intensity scores, other child-behaviour scales, parent outcomes, or later follow-up assessments. The requested effect is the raw mean difference (personalised minus standard non-personalised) in ECBI Problem scale points under a random-effects model; negative values favour the personalised intervention.
positive_direction: For sign-harmonised standardized effects, a positive value would mean that the personalised intervention reduces child conduct problems more than the standard non-personalised intervention. For the explicitly requested raw mean difference calculated as personalised minus standard, lower ECBI Problem scores are better and MD < 0 favours the personalised intervention.
search_queries: personalized tailored parenting intervention randomized ECBI Problem scale trial
adapted family intervention conduct problems ECBI controlled comparison
tailored parent training child behavior ECBI Problem randomized trial
inclusion_criteria: Original randomised trials enrolling children with conduct problems and evaluating a parenting or family intervention that is personalised, tailored, or adapted to an individual or subgroup.
Trials directly comparing the personalised intervention with an active, standard non-personalised version of the same intervention.

Trials reporting mother-reported ECBI Problem scale data at the first assessment after treatment ended, with post-treatment mean, SD (or convertible SE), and n per arm, or sufficient quantitative information to derive these values and the requested mean difference.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (exclude systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers), or completely unrelated to personalised parenting/family interventions for child conduct problems.

No randomised comparison between a personalised treatment and the standard non-personalised active version of the same intervention; this includes single-arm studies and comparisons against waitlist, usual care, no treatment, or an unrelated intervention.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size (e.g., no usable means plus SDs/SEs and sample sizes, t/F values, proportions, or odds ratios), including data unavailable after reasonable attempts to derive or obtain them.

Does not provide eligible mother-reported ECBI Problem scale results from the first post-treatment assessment; exclude ECBI Intensity scores, other behaviour scales, parent outcomes, and later follow-up-only results.
moderators_to_extract: Personalisation approach (individual tailoring versus subgroup adaptation)
Intervention format and delivery mode (individual/group; in-person/remote/hybrid)
Baseline conduct-problem severity and diagnostic/eligibility criteria
Risk-of-bias features, including allocation concealment and missing-outcome handling
effect_size_note: Use the post-treatment arm-level mean, SD, and n for the ECBI Problem scale at the first assessment after treatment ended. Prefer the mother's report if several reporters are presented. Convert SE to SD using SD = SE × sqrt(n). Compute MD as mean_personalised − mean_standard in ECBI Problem points and pool with a random-effects model; MD < 0 favours the personalised intervention. Do not pool follow-up assessments, ECBI Intensity scores, other behaviour scales, or parent outcomes.
single_outcome_target: child conduct problems on the ECBI Problem scale
